lane: tectonic geomorphology - channel steepness and knickpoints (chi / ksn), not scarp shape
hypothesis: Channels crossing a withheld fault segment carry a larger chi-normalised steepness step (relative ksn step) than random lines of the same orientation, once the lane brief's four confounds (playa base levels, ephemeral washes, lithology, climate gradient) are masked; and knickpoints corroborated by >= 3 independent first-order drainages along a common strike therefore locate faults the catalogue omits.
mechanism: Stream power: ksn = (U/K)^(1/n), so a step in rock uplift rate U across an active normal fault produces a RELATIVE (ratio) step in ksn at the crossing and upstream of it (Kirby & Whipple 2012, doi:10.1016/j.jsg.2012.07.009). The chi transform puts channels of different drainage area on one axis so those ratios are comparable between drainages (Perron & Royden 2013, doi:10.1002/esp.3302); the committed 10 m reduction segments the chi-z profile per Gailleton et al. (2019), doi:10.5194/esurf-7-211-2019.
named_non_fault_process_that_could_mimic: Steepness LEVEL, not steepness STEP. Mapped faults sit preferentially on range fronts, where channels are steep. Any statistic carrying the ksn level (absolute dksn, piedmont curvature, slope) inherits that. MEASURED: a statistic containing no step information at all - block-centred log(ksn) - scores +0.1946 [+0.1695, +0.2195] on the same first test (n=1823), which is larger than half the secondary arm's effect. Dipping resistant-over-weak lithology, debris-flow reaches and orographic discharge gradients are the other named mimics; the first two are masked, the third is block-detrended.

first_test.question: Do channels crossing withheld catalogue segments show larger steepness steps than random lines of the same orientation?
first_test.power_note: n = 4004 scoreable components vs n = 262 in every prior run of this lane (15x).
first_test.decision: STOP - the preregistered gate (mean > 0 AND lower 95% bound > 0) was not met by the primary statistic.
first_test.reading: The primary statistic is null at 15x the power of any prior run: +0.0097 log units [-0.0012, +0.0203], so the ksn ratio step at a withheld fault is bounded below ~2%. The median component is NEGATIVE (-0.0449) and only 40.4% of components are positive, so the small positive mean is a tail effect, not a systematic shift. On the population the board actually scores (off-catalogue SGMC structures) the same statistic is significantly NEGATIVE (-0.0851 [-0.0948, -0.0751]): those structures are relict, and channels crossing them are NOT steeper than background.

holdout_dti.interpretation: The lane surface is BELOW a mass-matched random control at every emission density (0.003475 vs 0.013561 at 8,811 px; 0.002412 vs 0.001865 at 1,091 px). A holdout DTI is not a leaderboard score and the catalogue instrument is not the board's off-catalogue population, but a field that cannot beat random dots on either population has no path to a competitive score.

leakage_verdict: CLEAN - every single feature alone is <= 0.6078 max(AUC, 1-AUC), far below the 0.90 trip level.

uniqueness.unsatisfiable_note: a registry raster whose own 3-px dilation already covers > 70% of the footprint makes the literal rule unsatisfiable for ANY candidate; these are calibration lattices and dense packings, not distinguishable submissions
